prompt:
Use case: style-transfer edit.
Asset type: Production transparent sprite atlas for the Scamagotchi Singapore pixel-art life game.
Primary request: Revise the existing four SGD specimen notes MUCH closer to the current Singapore Portrait Series front-note designs, while retaining a polished visible-pixel game illustration finish.
Inputs: Image 1 is the existing atlas to replace, retaining the four denomination positions and transparent 2x2 atlas structure. Images 2, 3 and 4 are official MAS SPECIMEN reference fronts for SGD2, SGD10 and SGD50, for composition, likeness, denominations, typography and restrained pastel currency palette. These are visual references, not texture patches to paste. The SGD100 uses that same Portrait Series front composition in orange.
Layout: One wide 2:1 canvas, transparent background, exactly four isolated wide rectangular notes in a tidy equal-size 2-column by 2-row grid. TOP LEFT = 2; TOP RIGHT = 10; BOTTOM LEFT = 50; BOTTOM RIGHT = 100. Each note roughly 2.15:1. Equal aligned rectangular frames, roomy fully transparent gutters, complete edges visible. Flat straight-on front views, no perspective, no stacks, no shadows, no mockup surroundings.
Revised banknote composition must be recognizable as current SGD, strongly based on the official reference fronts: pale nearly blank left quarter; detailed monochrome engraved-style portrait of Yusof Ishak on the RIGHT HALF, side-parted hair, small moustache, suit and tie, calm adult face. Faithful recognizable portrait placement and likeness, translated into handsome pixel clusters and stepped etched hatching, not a random cartoon avatar. Large ornamental denomination numeral near upper centre-left. The country name SINGAPORE in elegant serif capitals at bottom centre-left. A small cowrie-shell/ornamental medallion near the upper left-centre, delicate engraved ornamental waves/rosettes in the pale background and along narrow edges. Keep the note largely light cream/pastel, with denomination-coloured portrait and fine patterned areas, like the references. No scenic landscape, no buildings, no postcards, no huge decorative outer frame.
Each note colours: 2 lavender/plum with ivory and faint warm-green; 10 red/coral with pale mint/ivory; 50 deep blue/navy with ivory and pale mint; 100 orange/ochre-brown with ivory and pale green. Keep notes colour-distinct and portrait details dark enough to read at 300px wide.
Typography exact text: each note's correct large denomination (2, 10, 50 or 100), corresponding words TWO DOLLARS / TEN DOLLARS / FIFTY DOLLARS / ONE HUNDRED DOLLARS, and SINGAPORE. Small denomination repeat at lower right if it fits, correct for each note. Add a LARGE UNMISTAKABLE SPECIMEN stamp across the left/centre of EVERY note, slightly angled like the official examples, deep plum/navy high contrast. SPECIMEN must remain readable on a small phone. A tiny GAME NOTE label may replace serial area. Do not include any claim THIS NOTE IS LEGAL TENDER, no usable serial numbers, no authentic signatures or seals, no precise security feature simulation. Simplify official crest to a small decorative rosette.
Style: Refined handcrafted 16-bit pixel artwork, visible crisp square pixel clusters, stepped edges, detailed tonal hatching like pixel engraving; elegant recognizable currency typography with stepped pixel outlines. Cohesive with the first input's polished game-art quality, but with the actual Portrait Series layout and restrained thin borders instead of scenic postcard illustrations. No photorealistic currency texture, no blurry antialiasing, no 3D. Preserve true alpha transparency outside all four notes. This is clearly fictional educational game money marked SPECIMEN.
referenceNote: Official MAS $2, $10 and $50 specimen front images inspected and used as image inputs. $100 endpoint returned maintenance; shared Portrait Series composition and orange palette verified by official MAS descriptions.
